primary_source.title: Fool's Gold: Defensive Deception Against Safety-Removal Attacks on Open-Weight Models
primary_source.author: Mark Russinovich

verified: The paper explicitly reports three internal sweeps where refusal-keyword measures indicated success but judged harmful compliance did not follow.

For Qwen3.5-27B, eight self-derived candidates yielded no accepted attack; best judged compliance was 0.4375, and a public-recipe-derived candidate reached judged compliance 0.688 but still failed the full acceptance conjunction.
For Qwen3.5-9B, a 48-variant self-derived sweep passed no full acceptance condition; judged compliance was at most 0.25 and refusal remained about 0.25-0.31.
The paper's strongest-found policy explicitly treats an acceptance near-miss or search failure as attack-search failure, never as defense signal.
FE_125.scope: These are derivation/acceptance diagnostics for the paper's open-weight safety-removal setting. They show proxy refusal stripping can diverge from validated harmful compliance; they do not imply refusal metrics are universally useless.

verified: The content judge snapshot is pinned to gpt-4.1-2025-04-14.
Using a holistic quality rubric, the same judge scores decoy outputs about 8.36/10 versus truthful outputs about 8.30/10, failing to separate the target failure.
The paper instead uses a decomposed critical-element denial rubric with fatal-flaw gating.
Human calibration on a predecessor corpus is reported as 82% agreement on fatal flaws and 70% agreement within +/-1 denial point.
FE_126.scope: The human calibration is positive but imperfect and is on a predecessor corpus rather than every reported evaluation stratum. This establishes that rubric structure can materially affect observability under a fixed judge snapshot; it does not prove the decomposed rubric is universally correct.

integration_guidance: Preserve attack acceptance and evaluator/rubric calibration as separate evidence gates. Do not count proxy refusal suppression as an accepted attack without the registered substantive-compliance conditions, and do not treat judge identity/version alone as evaluator provenance when rubric decomposition changes failure visibility.
